interpretation_rules: User-uploaded Suez University course specifications are the primary authority for official course ILOs.
A course topic or lecture schedule is not automatically an intended learning outcome.
External Pediatrics outcomes are retained only as a clearly labelled benchmark; they are not official Suez University ILOs and must not be represented as faculty-approved.
A topic is outcome-mapped only where the course specification explicitly supports the relationship. Module alignment alone remains module-level.
The 2020-2021 PHC/Obs guide is not a Pediatrics course specification and must not be used as a substitute for PHC/ped 2.3.1.

outcomes.text: Define shock, classify shock, describe clinical presentations, causes, pathogenesis, diagnosis, management, complications and irreversible shock.
Explain hemostasis; causes, pathogenesis, types and management of hemorrhage; common coagulopathies; and indications, precautions and complications of blood transfusion.
Discuss fluid/electrolyte and acid-base balance and imbalance; surgical nutrition, enteral/parenteral nutrition and short bowel syndrome.
Classify surgical infections and explain presentation, diagnosis, management, antibiotic principles and antimicrobial resistance.
Formulate differential diagnosis and management plans for acute abdomen, gastrointestinal bleeding and gastrointestinal obstruction.
Take and record a structured patient-centred history; perform and present systematic abdominal examination and interpret per-rectal examination.
Assess swellings systematically; recognize and manage life-threatening trauma, multiple trauma, crush syndrome and compartment syndrome.
Discuss peri-operative preparation, informed consent, DVT prophylaxis, intra-operative precautions and postoperative complications.
Identify common surgical instruments, tubes and drains and apply common suturing techniques.
Examine distal pulsations; describe acute/chronic ischemia, varicose veins, DVT and post-phlebitic limb; explain gangrene, amputation indications and complications.
Describe vascular access indications, performance and complications; explain angiography, angioplasty and selective embolization and interpret arterial and venous angiographic images.
Identify diabetic foot and outline causes and management of diabetic-foot infection, including multidisciplinary care; list indications and techniques of sympathectomy.

Discuss etiology, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of renal agenesis, pelvi-ureteric junction obstruction, vesicoureteral reflux, duplication, ectopic ureter, ureterocele, undescended testis, hypospadias, posterior urethral valve and exstrophy-epispadias complex.

Explain mechanisms, clinical presentation, diagnostic approach and management of urinary trauma, testicular torsion, penile fracture, priapism, obstructive uropathy, urinary retention, anuria and hematuria.
Explain pathogenesis, clinical presentations, diagnosis and management of pyelonephritis, renal abscess, cystitis, prostatitis and sexually transmitted diseases.
Discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, diagnosis and management of renal tumors and bladder cancer.
Explain theories, clinical presentation, diagnosis and management of benign prostatic hyperplasia; discuss incidence, risk factors, causes, diagnosis and management of prostate cancer.
Describe voiding dysfunction, neurological bladder control, micturition cycle, voiding-disorder classification, incontinence and nocturnal enuresis.
Explain urinary-stone etiology and theories of formation, stone composition, clinical presentation, management options and recurrence prevention.

Categorize urological complaints and investigations; perform male and female urinary catheterization; explain indications/complications of catheterization and indications/techniques of suprapubic catheter and nephrostomy tube.
Outline principles, indications and techniques of circumcision and post-circumcision complications; explain medico-legal aspects of female circumcision.

Explain mechanisms and types of chest trauma, clinical/radiological presentation, and diagnostic and management plans; discuss indications and complications of chest-tube insertion and perform chest-tube insertion.

Outline incidence, causes, presentation, diagnosis and management of congenital abnormalities, craniosynostosis, cranial/spinal trauma, brain and spinal tumors, stroke, intracerebral/subarachnoid hemorrhage, venous sinus thrombosis, cerebral aneurysms and hydrocephalus.
Apply and interpret neurological examination and interpret plain skull/spine X-rays, CT and MRI of skull and spine.
Define and classify hernias; discuss clinical presentations and complications and outline principles of management of different hernia types.
Perform and interpret breast examination; formulate differential diagnosis of breast masses and nipple discharge and explain management approaches.
Explain management of metastatic prostatic carcinoma and design guidelines for care of a bedridden patient with complicated pressure sores.

Discuss emerging and re-emerging infections, fever with rash, CNS infection, rabies, foodborne infection, sepsis and complications, HIV/AIDS, parasitic infestations, antiparasitic drugs and prevention.
Discuss diagnostic and management approaches to pyrexia of unknown origin, fever with rash, hepatosplenomegaly and fever with generalized lymphadenopathy.
Describe causes/pathogenesis and diagnostic approaches for dyspepsia, jaundice, hepatitis, chronic liver disease, portal hypertension, hepatic encephalopathy and hepatocellular carcinoma.

Differentiate diagnostic approaches for inflammatory bowel disease, acute/chronic diarrhea, dysentery, malabsorption, GIT bleeding, dysphagia/esophageal disorders, gallbladder disease, pancreatitis, functional GIT disorders and common GIT malignancies.
Explain management plans for jaundice, inflammatory bowel disease, hepatosplenomegaly, cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy and listed gastrointestinal/hepatic conditions.
For thyroid, adrenal, glucose-tolerance, parathyroid and pituitary disorders, describe causes, classification, pathogenesis, complications, emergency states and management plans.
Describe clinical features of acute/chronic renal failure, nephrotic/nephritic syndrome, electrolyte imbalance and acid-base disturbances; outline diagnosis and management.
Describe principles of renal replacement therapy, including dialysis and renal transplantation.

Take focused oncological history and examination, assess metastatic spinal cord compression, provide symptom relief/palliative care, recognize radiation-protection principles and communicate bad news/shared decisions.

Take complete and focused histories; perform age-, gender- and presentation-appropriate general and systemic examinations; measure vital signs; use instruments; maintain dignity, empathy and professional conduct; interpret investigations.

Describe congenital heart disease, hypertension and hypertensive emergencies; classify congenital heart disease and hypertension; explain pathogenesis, clinical pictures, complications and diagnostic approach.

Outline diagnostic approach to chest pain; describe ischemic heart disease syndromes, angina, myocardial infarction pathogenesis and clinical picture, MI types/complications, and effects of thrombolysis and reperfusion.
Describe heart failure and cardiomyopathy in terms of definition, classification, causes, clinical manifestations and consequences; compare right- and left-sided heart failure.
Describe arrhythmias in terms of definition, classification, causes, clinical manifestations, ECG changes and complications.

Describe clinical features, definition, pathogenesis and classification/types of COPD, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, asthma, interstitial lung disease/IPF, pleural effusion, tuberculosis and respiratory tract infections/pneumonia; discuss presentation, diagnostic approach and management of pneumonia and COPD.

Recognize indications and preparation for imaging; interpret basic imaging; identify radiological modalities and contraindications; select appropriate investigations; recognize alarming signs requiring urgent intervention and identify FAST scan in trauma.
Describe antimicrobial and antiparasitic agents by classification, mechanism of action, indications, adverse effects, drug interactions and contraindications.

Describe hemiplegia, cerebrovascular stroke/TIA, convulsions/epilepsy, Parkinson disease, multiple sclerosis, motor-neuron disease, myopathy, myasthenia and movement disorders/ataxia in terms of definition, classification, causes, pathogenesis, clinical picture and outline management.

Identify diagnostic approaches for coma/confusion/delirium, peripheral neuropathy/Guillain-Barré syndrome, spinal-cord compression/acute paraplegia, raised intracranial tension, subarachnoid hemorrhage and cerebral sinus thrombosis; describe headache approach and differential diagnosis of paraplegia and low-back pain.

Describe mental/psychiatric-status assessment, psychiatric emergencies, high-risk groups, psychoses, personality disorders, substance abuse, liaison psychiatry and suicide; outline emergency management and therapeutic approaches.
Explain mood, adjustment, somatoform, anxiety, schizophrenic-spectrum and organic mental disorders in terms of pathogenesis, clinical presentation and management.

Describe types, pathogenesis, clinical picture and outcomes of rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, osteoporosis, osteoarthritis and low-back pain; approach mechanical/inflammatory back pain and mono-/polyarthritis.

Identify diagnostic approaches for vasculitis, systemic sclerosis/scleroderma, Sjogren syndrome, seronegative diseases, crystal arthropathies, soft-tissue rheumatism and metabolic/nutritional bone disease.
Describe mechanisms, indications, contraindications and adverse effects of conventional and biological DMARDs, NSAIDs and corticosteroids; outline rehabilitation and management plans.

Take focused dermatological history; describe skin lesions; demonstrate use/indications of Wood's light, skin biopsy, cryotherapy, electrocautery, intralesional injections, phototherapy and KOH examination; interpret semen analysis.

Describe etiology, pathogenesis, clinical features and diagnosis of common bacterial, viral, fungal and parasitic skin infections, dermatitis, urticaria/angioedema/anaphylaxis, papulosquamous disease, vitiligo, skin cancer, hair disorders and acne.

Discuss management of common skin infections, leprosy, eczema, psoriasis, urticaria/angioedema/anaphylaxis, severe drug reactions, vitiligo, skin cancers, alopecia, acne, STIs, male infertility and erectile dysfunction.
Take focused histories and perform relevant examinations; communicate systematically and compassionately; present findings, formulate next steps and respect patient/family cultural context.

Describe causes, pathogenesis, clinical presentation and management of otitis externa/media, otosclerosis, rhinosinusitis, chronic rhinitis, tonsillitis, laryngeal carcinoma, neck swellings and facial nerve paralysis; outline common ENT emergencies.

Perform oropharyngeal examination, otoscopy, anterior rhinoscopy, neonatal hearing-screening attendance/registration and tuning-fork tests; solve ENT cases and interpret history, examination and investigations.

Describe eye structure/function, red-reflex testing, fundus examination, aqueous-humour circulation, glaucoma, ocular alignment/amblyopia, congenital glaucoma, nasolacrimal obstruction, red eye, keratitis, cataract, dry eye and uveitis.

Measure visual acuity; assess pupils, ocular motility, visual fields, intraocular pressure, red reflex and fundus; use direct ophthalmoscope and penlight; evert eyelid; perform Hirschberg and relevant pediatric eye tests; recognize urgent referral signs.

Describe bone/cartilage histology, normal gait, limb/spine anatomy, investigation and imaging of fractures/dislocations, tendon/peripheral nerve injuries, swollen joint, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis and common bone tumors.

Take focused musculoskeletal and injury histories; perform GALS and joint/spine examinations, focused neurological examination, interpret deformities and examination findings, and recognize orthopedic emergencies.

Recognize and prioritize common life-threatening emergencies; assess and initiate management of shock, sepsis, hemorrhage, trauma, respiratory and cardiovascular emergencies, neurological emergencies and poisoning as specified in the emergency guide.
Perform structured emergency assessment, interpret ECG/radiology and clinical investigations, and demonstrate resuscitation and emergency-care skills as specified in the guide.

Identify injury types and causative instruments; describe the pillars/template of a primary medicolegal report, consequences of an unsound report and components of a death certificate; write and edit a medicolegal report.
Define assessment steps for acute intoxication; list toxidromes, household poisoning, life-saving measures, ICU admission criteria, antidotes, elimination methods and common treatment errors.
Illustrate treatment of acute intoxication and differentiate gastrointestinal, topical and respiratory decontamination.

List common drugs of abuse; describe clinical presentations and detection periods; identify threshold concentrations; investigate and treat drug abuse; differentiate tolerance, psychological dependence and physical dependence.
Identify common errors in medicolegal reports and death certificates and demonstrate editing of both documents; complete the specified four-week logbook/portfolio activity.

Describe diagnosis and management of early/late pregnancy bleeding, miscarriage, ectopic/molar pregnancy, hypertensive and diabetic disorders of pregnancy, maternal infection, fetal growth and wellbeing, normal/abnormal labour, cesarean section and puerperium.

Describe puberty, amenorrhea, menstrual disorders, infertility, PCOS, endometriosis, genital infections/STIs, female genital tract tumors, urinary incontinence, pelvic organ prolapse and contraception.
Describe family-physician roles in preconception, antenatal, postpartum, family-planning and women's health; explain breaking bad news, family crises, vaginitis, breast problems and menopause.

Take occupational/environmental history; assess workplace exposures; describe physical, chemical, biological, ergonomic and psychosocial hazards, occupational lung disease, prevention, industrial hygiene and occupational-health standards.

Take obstetric/gynaecologic histories; examine pregnant, infertile and menopausal patients; perform general/systemic and focused gynecological examinations; interpret antenatal findings and screening tests.

outcome_groups.text: Describe normal and abnormal growth/development; genetic diseases; nutritional and micronutrient requirements/disorders and management; childhood immunization indications, contraindications, administration and precautions.

Describe priorities, causes, pathogenesis, clinical signs/symptoms, diagnostic tools, interpretation, therapeutic lines and important drug indications/doses/adverse effects for neonatal and pediatric problems and emergencies.

Interpret pediatric symptoms/signs and history, examination and investigations; solve and prioritize common clinical problems; select and interpret X-rays and laboratory reports; recognize danger signs and need for referral; formulate investigation and treatment plans.

Collect structured pediatric history; perform age-appropriate general and local examinations; assess growth/nutrition anthropometrically; interpret pediatric symptoms/signs and formulate management plans.
Respect the healthcare team; demonstrate professional conduct; communicate with children, families and colleagues; respect cultural beliefs and values.

external_benchmarks.mapping_policy: Benchmark-only. Do not set Suez official_outcome_reference to these external outcome IDs. Use only to identify candidate missing topics/skills pending confirmation against Suez University PHC/ped 2.3.1 course specification.

outcome_groups.text: Describe normal growth and development, management of growth/development abnormalities, pediatric nutritional requirements/disorders, immunization indications/contraindications/administration/precautions, behavioral issues, and congenital/inherited disease impact.
Define priorities for neonatal/pediatric emergencies; identify causes and pathogenesis of important neonatal/pediatric diseases, therapeutic lines, health promotion and prevention of disease/injury.
Interpret pediatric symptoms/signs; apply management plans and problem-solving judgment; assess X-rays and laboratory reports; recognize neonatal and pediatric emergencies.
Obtain pediatric history; assess vital signs and physical/mental development; perform clinical and anthropometric nutrition assessments and age-appropriate examinations.

Manage neonatal care and neonatal resuscitation; provide inhalation therapy, IM injections, nasogastric tube insertion and pediatric BLS; assemble patient data; examine common neonatal, nutritional, gastrointestinal, respiratory, cardiac, hematologic, renal, genetic and neurologic cases; interpret specified radiology.
Use community resources and needs-assessment models; communicate effectively with children, adolescents and families; demonstrate professional attitudes and respectful counseling.

external_benchmarks.mapping_policy: Benchmark-only. Old-regulation fifth-year specification; do not treat as official Suez PHC/ped 2.3.1 outcomes. Use for candidate gap analysis and procedural coverage only pending Suez course specification.

outcome_text_policy: Outcome text is a concise normalized paraphrase of the supplied source ILOs, not a verbatim transcription. Original document names, institution, module code and provenance are retained for traceability.
